columns.name: Memory platform
columns.instruction: Record the physical system used as the quantum memory at the nodes. If the two nodes use different platforms, select both. Choose 'Other' only if none of the listed systems fits.

columns.name: Heralding scheme
columns.instruction: Record how the remote entanglement is heralded, as described by the authors. Select every scheme that applies to the main demonstration. Choose 'Unclear' if the source does not describe the scheme well enough to classify it.

columns.name: Fibre link length
columns.instruction: Give the length of optical fibre (or free-space channel) between each memory node and the heralding station, or the total link length, exactly as stated. Copy the source's wording into as_stated so it is clear which length is meant. If several lengths are tested, take the one used for the main reported entanglement result.

columns.name: Node separation
columns.instruction: Give the physical distance between the two memory nodes as stated, for example the distance between the labs. Do not use the fibre length here. If several separations are tested, take the one used for the main reported entanglement result. If the authors do not single out a main result, mark the column unknown.

columns.name: Bell-state fidelity
columns.instruction: Give the fidelity of the heralded remote entangled state with respect to the target maximally entangled Bell state, for the main demonstration. Include the uncertainty in as_stated if given. If only a lower bound is reported, give it and keep the wording such as '≥' in as_stated. If fidelities are given separately for different heralded Bell states and no combined value is stated, mark the column unknown.

columns.name: Herald rate
columns.instruction: Give the rate of successful entanglement heralding events, as stated, for the main entanglement demonstration. Do not use the attempt rate or the success probability per attempt. If only a success probability per attempt is given, leave the column unknown. If several configurations are reported and the authors do not single out a main one, mark it unknown.

columns.name: Telecom frequency conversion
columns.instruction: Answer yes if the photons used for heralding are converted to a telecom wavelength (e.g. O- or C-band) before transmission. Answer no if the source states that photons are sent at the memory's native wavelength without conversion. If the source does not settle this, mark it unknown.

columns.name: Entangled-state storage time
columns.instruction: Give the time for which the heralded remote entanglement is preserved in the memories as reported. This can be a coherence time of the entangled state, the longest storage time at which entanglement is still verified, or the time at which fidelity drops to a stated threshold. Put the source's own wording in as_stated so the definition stays visible. Do not use single-memory coherence times measured without remote entanglement. If no such time is reported in the inspected passages, mark the column not found.

columns.name: Entanglement verification method
columns.instruction: Record how the authors verify the heralded remote entanglement and obtain the reported fidelity in the main demonstration. Select every method used. Choose 'Other' only if none of the listed methods fits. Choose 'Unclear' if the source does not describe the verification well enough to classify it.

options.label: Correlation measurements in two or more bases (e.g. parity oscillations)

columns.name: Success probability per attempt
columns.instruction: Give the probability of a successful entanglement herald per attempt, as stated, for the main entanglement demonstration. Keep the source's wording, such as '1e-4' or '0.01 %', in as_stated. If several configurations are reported and the authors do not single out a main one, mark the column unknown.

columns.name: Fidelity correction
columns.instruction: State whether the main reported Bell-state fidelity is the raw measured value or is corrected, for example for detector dark counts, background or readout errors. Choose 'Both reported' if the source gives raw and corrected values. Choose 'Not stated' if the source does not say.

options.label: Corrected (e.g. for background, dark counts or readout errors)

columns.name: Photonic qubit encoding
columns.instruction: Record the degree of freedom in which the heralding photons carry the memory–photon entanglement in the main demonstration. Select every encoding used. Choose 'Unclear' if the source does not say.

columns.name: Number of entangled nodes
columns.instruction: Record how many memory nodes share the heralded entanglement in the main demonstration. Count only nodes holding quantum memories, not the heralding station.

columns.name: Photon wavelength at heralding station
columns.instruction: Give the wavelength of the photons as they arrive at the heralding station (after any frequency conversion), as stated. If the two nodes send different wavelengths, mark the column unknown and say so in the note.

columns.name: Attempt rate
columns.instruction: Give the rate at which entanglement generation attempts are made (the repetition rate of the protocol), as stated, for the main entanglement demonstration. Do not use the rate of successful heralds. If several configurations are reported and the authors do not single out a main one, mark the column unknown.

columns.name: Entanglement faster than decoherence
columns.instruction: Answer yes if the source states that remote entanglement is heralded faster than it decays in the memories (for example a link efficiency above one, or herald rate exceeding the decoherence rate). Answer no if the source states that it is not. If the source does not address this, mark the column unknown.

Record the matter degree of freedom that stores the remote entanglement in the main demonstration. Select every encoding used, for example when the qubit is first held in one state and then moved to another for storage. Choose 'Other' only if none of the listed encodings fits. Choose 'Unclear' if the source does not say.
columns.name: Memory qubit encoding

options.label: Hyperfine or Zeeman ground-state levels of atoms or ions
Electron spin of a defect or quantum dot
Collective spin-wave excitation of an ensemble

columns.rationale: The storage time of the entangled state depends strongly on which matter degree of freedom holds the qubit, so this helps compare the storage times the question asks for.

columns.instruction: Record whether the fibre between the nodes and the heralding station is installed outside the laboratory (deployed field or metropolitan fibre), wound on spools in the laboratory, or a mix of both, for the main demonstration. Choose 'Not applicable' if the photons travel in free space or only through short in-lab patch fibres. Choose 'Not stated' if the source does not say.
columns.name: Fibre deployment

options.label: Mix of deployed and spooled fibre
Not applicable (free space or short in-lab fibre only)

columns.rationale: Whether the herald rate and fidelity were reached over real deployed fibre or over spools is needed to compare the experiments fairly.

columns.instruction: Answer yes if the source states that a technique to extend memory coherence is applied while the remote entangled state is stored. Examples are dynamical decoupling pulses, transfer to a magnetically insensitive or clock transition, or transfer to a nuclear-spin memory. Answer no if the source states that the entangled state is stored without such protection. If the source does not settle this, mark it unknown.
columns.name: Coherence protection during storage
columns.rationale: Reported storage times of the entangled state are only comparable if it is known whether coherence-protection techniques were used.

columns.instruction: Give the fidelity of the entangled state between one memory and its emitted photon, measured at a single node before or apart from the remote heralding, as stated. If the two nodes report different values and no combined value is stated, mark the column unknown. If several values are given, take the one the authors associate with the main remote entanglement demonstration. Keep the uncertainty or wording such as '≥' in as_stated.
columns.name: Memory–photon entanglement fidelity
columns.rationale: The single-node memory–photon fidelity bounds the achievable remote Bell-state fidelity and helps explain differences in the fidelities the question asks about.

columns.instruction: Give the number of temporal, spectral or spatial modes used in parallel per entanglement generation attempt in the main demonstration, as stated. If the scheme uses a single mode per attempt and the source says so, give 1. If several mode numbers are tested and the authors do not single out a main one, mark the column unknown.
columns.name: Multiplexed modes
columns.rationale: Multiplexing directly raises the herald rate, so it is needed to interpret the reported herald rates.

columns.instruction: Give the overall probability that a photon emitted by one memory is detected at the heralding station (end-to-end or link efficiency, including collection, transmission, any conversion and detection), as stated for the main demonstration. If the two nodes report different values and no combined or typical value is stated, mark the column unknown. Do not use detector efficiency alone.
columns.name: Photon detection efficiency per node
columns.rationale: End-to-end photon efficiency sets the success probability and herald rate and makes the rates comparable across platforms.

columns.instruction: Answer yes if the source states that the stored remote entanglement can be read out or used at a time chosen after the herald, for example by triggered retrieval or by keeping the qubit until a feed-forward signal arrives. Answer no if the source states that readout happens at a fixed, preset delay regardless of the herald. If the source does not settle this, mark it unknown.
columns.name: On-demand retrieval
columns.rationale: Whether the entangled state can be held and used on demand shows what the reported storage time of the entangled state means in practice.

columns.instruction: Record any task the authors carry out using the heralded remote entanglement in the source, beyond verifying it. Select every task that applies. Choose 'None beyond verification' if the entanglement is only characterised. Choose 'Other' only if none of the listed tasks fits.
columns.name: Protocol demonstrated with the entanglement

options.label: Entanglement swapping or repeater segment extension

columns.rationale: Knowing what each experiment used its entanglement for gives context for the herald rates, fidelities and storage times reported.

column_suggestions.notes: The suggestions avoid the sixteen existing columns. They add context needed to compare herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time across experiments: memory qubit encoding, coherence protection, multiplexing, efficiency, fibre deployment, on-demand use and downstream protocols. No rows were supplied, so the options rely on general knowledge of the field, not on the table's sources.
